notes: LORE.md 1c: the six fragments. Tucker Gold's own holo recordings,
flattened to tape by Shepard when the player brings one in. His
life in order: what he was, her, her death, the copy, putting the
power down, and an old man talking to whoever eventually asks.
* she is never named, and her nation is never named. The place is
* no dates. Non-corporeal immortals do not file timestamps;
* no Q. He has never heard of Starfleet, or of anybody watching;
* his name is in five, because five is where he takes it;
* six is to "whoever found this", never to the player by name.
title: Fragment one: what I was
subtitle: A holo recording, three hundred years old
author: dubbed to tape by Lt. Shepard
extra: One of six. He numbered them himself.

lines.text: DUBBED FROM HOLO -- FRAGMENT ONE OF SIX
Flattened to two dimensions. It loses the depth. Sorry.
An old man in a chair by a window. The light is morning.
This is the first. I am going to do them in order.
Whoever finds these may not find them in order. Well.
I was not always a man. I was not always anything.
I was a thing that went from place to place. Looking.
You would not have seen me. You would have felt weather.
There are others of my kind. We do not keep company.
We have nothing to say to each other. We are too alike.
He laughs, once, and it turns into a cough.
I could make things. Anything. A house, a forest, a sea.
And unmake them. I want you to know that I could.
It matters to the rest of this, that I could.
I came to your people because you die.
Nothing I had ever known died. Stars, but not quickly.
You were born and you were gone, and in between you
did the most extraordinary things, in such a hurry.
I watched for a long time. I did not interfere.
I thought watching was a kind of respect.
I thought a great many things, then.
He looks out of the window. Something outside, a river.
That is the first. The next one is about her.
-- FRAGMENT ONE ENDS --
